title: Kernel-fusion guided KV segmentation and soft-evict hysteresis for low-jitter prefill
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: On mixed tenant workloads the paged KV cache exhibits jittery prefill latency when the kernel selection logic switches between narrow and fused kernel paths. This causes tail latency spikes for short-lived interactive requests. Goal: Reduce prefill jitter and improve 99th percentile decode latency by coordinating kernel fusion preferences with KV segmentation (hot vs. cold segments) and a soft-evict hysteresis window. Approach: 1) Add a lightweight runtime hint that tags KV segments with a kernel-fusion score (based on recent decode patterns, sequence length histograms, and kernel warmness). 2) Use fusion scores to bias placement: group segments that benefit from fused multi-head kernels into contiguous reservation lanes to preserve co-location and avoid frequent kernel swaps. 3) Implement a soft-evict hysteresis (time+access-count) so segments predicted to be re-used soon are temporarily resistant to eviction; eviction only proceeds after hysteresis expiry or when a global pressure threshold is crossed. 4) Integrate this with prefill admission: prefill admission favors co-located segments enabling a single kernel selection for a prefilling microbatch. Trade-offs: increases metadata accounting (fusion score) and slightly reduces maximum packing density; but expected to lower kernel-awareness thrashing and reduce tail latency. Success criteria: - Reduce prefill-induced kernel switches per-second by >=40% on synthetic mixed-length traces. - Improve decode P99 by >=15% on interactive trace (same QPS). - No >5% regression in average throughput for heavy streaming workloads. Metrics: kernel_switch_rate, prefill_latency_P50/P95/P99, eviction_recycles_per_min, reuse_ratio (hit rate within hysteresis), GPU occupancy. Implementation phases: A: runtime hint + segment scoring (2w); B: segment grouping allocator + lane reservation (2w); C: soft-evict hysteresis + admission policy (2w); D: benchmarks and telemetry + canary rollout (1w).
